claims: NASA is set to launch Artemis II no earlier than April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center.
Artemis II is the first crewed Moon mission since 1972.
Four astronauts will conduct a 10-day around-the-moon test flight for Artemis II.
Live coverage of Artemis II is available via NASA+, YouTube, and Amazon Prime.
Artemis II mission goal is a 10-day crewed test flight around the Moon.
Artemis II tests the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule.
Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Primary launch window for Artemis II opens on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II launch has an 80% chance of favorable weather.
Artemis II launch weather monitoring is primarily for clouds and wind.
Artemis II crew will fly beyond the Moon, perform a U-turn, and return.
Artemis II launch is expected to be visible from parts of Florida and southern Georgia.
Artemis III is planned as the first human landing in this program.
Artemis III aims to land astronauts on the lunar surface.
Artemis III has potential adjustments in strategy and timing to ensure safety.
SpaceX is developing the Starship Human Landing System.
SpaceX is targeting uncrewed lunar landing tests in 2027.
